uBpazmjT1kc.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 27: Workshop on Similar Verses (Adh-Dhariyat and Al-Ma'arij)
uBpazmjT1kc.one_line: A group exercise comparing two similar passages: the muhsinin of Adh-Dhariyat who go beyond, and the musallin of Al-Ma'arij who keep the minimum.
uBpazmjT1kc.summary: The speaker shows that clusters of verses that sound alike, which reciters often confuse, are never random. He gives four tools for comparing them: context before and after, keywords, subtle differences in wording and word order, and the occasion of revelation, noting that Arabic fronts what matters most, as in 'You alone we worship'. Groups then compare Adh-Dhariyat 51:15-19 with Al-Ma'arij 70:19-35. In Adh-Dhariyat the muhsinin, people who go the extra mile, sleep little at night, seek forgiveness before dawn, and give the asker and the deprived an unspecified right in their wealth. In Al-Ma'arij the anxious, grasping human is excepted only if he is one of the musallin, a noun describing people whose identity is prayer: they keep it constantly, recognise a known right of others in their wealth, believe in the Day of Judgment, are deeply concerned about their Lord's punishment, guard their chastity, keep trusts and covenants, uphold testimony and protect their prayers. He concludes that Al-Ma'arij sets the floor no believer may fall below, while Adh-Dhariyat describes a higher rank of voluntary excellence, and urges reading the Quran slowly with attention to such differences.

outline.heading: Similar clusters at the end of the Quran
outline.gist: Some passages share wording and even verse length but are not identical; the exercise is to find out why.

outline.heading: Interlude
Not random: look at the context
outline.gist: Reciters confuse such passages; first assume a reason and read what comes before and after.

outline.heading: Keywords and subtle differences
outline.gist: Each cluster has a keyword that Allah builds on, and the wording differs in small, meaningful ways.

outline.heading: The keyword of each passage
outline.gist: One passage builds on the muhsinin, the other on the human being and his description.

outline.heading: Occasion of revelation and word order
outline.gist: Arabic fronts what is most important, as in 'You alone we worship' rather than 'we worship You'.

outline.heading: Interlude
They slept little of the night
outline.gist: Fronting 'little' emphasizes how little they slept, spending the night in prayer and dua.

outline.heading: Seeking forgiveness before dawn
outline.gist: The same fronting highlights that the pre-dawn hours are given to istighfar.

outline.heading: A right, but not a known right
outline.gist: Adh-Dhariyat says 'a right' for the asker and the deprived, while Al-Ma'arij says 'a known right': voluntary giving versus the fixed obligation.

outline.heading: Muhsinin: those who go the extra mile
outline.gist: Ihsan always describes doing more than required, such as staying up at night and giving without counting.

outline.heading: Read slowly and look before and after
outline.gist: Reciting is not enough; contemplate the verse, the page before and the page after.

outline.heading: The anxious human being
outline.gist: The insan is never praised in the Quran: impatient, despairing in hardship and withholding in ease.

outline.heading: Except the musallin: prayer as identity
outline.gist: The noun musallin, rather than 'those who pray', describes people so constant in prayer that it defines them.

outline.heading: Constant in their prayer
outline.gist: Their day is scheduled around the prayer times.

outline.heading: A known right in their wealth
outline.gist: Part of every income belongs to someone else; the sunnah fixes it at two and a half percent for the asker and the deprived.

outline.heading: Interlude
From outward practice to inner belief
outline.gist: These verses set the bare minimum; after the physical practices come what they believe.

outline.heading: Believing in the Day of Judgment
outline.gist: Belief in accountability is what keeps a person from despair in hardship and stinginess in ease.

outline.heading: Concerned about their Lord's punishment
outline.gist: Mushfiqun means ongoing concern, which differs from simple fear.

outline.heading: Guarding chastity
outline.gist: No relationships outside what Islam permits; those who seek beyond it are transgressors who cross the line.

outline.heading: Keeping trusts and covenants
outline.gist: The amanah the heavens and mountains declined includes every covenant with Allah and every trust between people.

outline.heading: None of these may be broken
outline.gist: Unlike night prayer, these qualities are not optional; truthful testimony is among them.

outline.heading: Beginning and ending with prayer
outline.gist: The passage opens with constancy in prayer and closes with guarding it, and its people are honoured in gardens.

outline.heading: Which group ranks higher?
outline.gist: The muhsinin go above and beyond and rank higher; the musallin describe the floor no believer can go below.

outline.heading: Another similar cluster and repeated stories
outline.gist: The opening of Al-Mu'minun sounds similar again; repeated stories such as Nuh and Adam are each worded differently for a reason.

outline.heading: Interlude
Question: is the fuller description lower?
outline.gist: A questioner notes Al-Ma'arij lists more qualities; he answers that its items are obligatory, while the muhsinin give without limit.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: Similar passages are deliberate; reading slowly and comparing them reveals different messages.

themes.label: Methodology: how to read texts, tafsir method, intellectual approach
themes.note: Context, keywords, subtle wording differences, word order and occasion of revelation as tools for comparison.

themes.label: Ihsan and excellence in worship
themes.note: The muhsinin go beyond obligation: little sleep, pre-dawn istighfar and giving without counting.

themes.label: Salah: its meaning, etiquette and significance
themes.note: Prayer as identity: the musallin are defined by constant, guarded prayer.

themes.label: Zakat, charity and giving
themes.note: A known portion of wealth belongs to others and is not ours to keep.

themes.label: Accountability before Allah and goals
themes.note: Belief in judgment and concern about punishment keep a person steady in hardship and ease.

themes.label: Oaths, promises, trust and loyalty
themes.note: Chastity, trusts, covenants and truthful testimony are non-negotiable qualities of the believer.

quran.point: Fronting 'You alone' shows Arabic places the most important element first.
The trust offered to the heavens, earth and mountains, which they declined.
Another passage that sounds like the Al-Ma'arij description, left for listeners to compare.

maxims: In Arabic we start with what is important
Muhsin: the one who goes the extra mile
Similar is never random
takeaways: When two passages sound alike, compare their context, keywords, wording and order instead of mixing them up.
Treat the qualities in Al-Ma'arij as the floor: constant prayer, the due right in your wealth, chastity, trustworthiness and truthful testimony.
Aim above the floor with the muhsinin's voluntary night prayer, pre-dawn istighfar and generous giving.
Read the Quran slowly, looking at what comes before and after each verse.

2:184.ar: أَيَّامࣰ ا مَّعۡدُودَٰتࣲۚ فَمَن كَانَ مِنكُم مَّرِيضًا أَوۡ عَلَىٰ سَفَرࣲ فَعِدَّةࣱ مِّنۡ أَيَّامٍ أُخَرَۚ وَعَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ يُطِيقُونَهُۥ فِدۡيَةࣱ طَعَامُ مِسۡكِينࣲۖ فَمَن تَطَوَّعَ خَيۡرࣰ ا فَهُوَ خَيۡرࣱ لَّهُۥۚ وَأَن تَصُومُواْ خَيۡرࣱ لَّكُمۡ إِن كُنتُمۡ تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:184.en: [Fasting for] a limited number of days. So whoever among you is ill or on a journey [during them] - then an equal number of days [are to be made up]. And upon those who are able [to fast, but with hardship] - a ransom [as substitute] of feeding a poor person [each day]. And whoever volunteers excess - it is better for him. But to fast is best for you, if you only knew

97:3.ar: لَيۡلَةُ ٱلۡقَدۡرِ خَيۡرࣱ مِّنۡ أَلۡفِ شَهۡرࣲ‏
97:3.en: The Night of Decree is better than a thousand months

4:48.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَغۡفِرُ أَن يُشۡرَكَ بِهِۦ وَيَغۡفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن يَشَآءُۚ وَمَن يُشۡرِكۡ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدِ ٱفۡتَرَىٰٓ إِثۡمًا عَظِيمًا
4:48.en: Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And he who associates others with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin

62:10.ar: فَإِذَا قُضِيَتِ ٱلصَّلَوٰةُ فَٱنتَشِرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱبۡتَغُواْ مِن فَضۡلِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱذۡكُرُواْ ٱللَّهَ كَثِيرࣰ ا لَّعَلَّكُمۡ تُفۡلِحُونَ
62:10.en: And when the prayer has been concluded, disperse within the land and seek from the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah often that you may succeed

67:15.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِي جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ ذَلُولࣰ ا فَٱمۡشُواْ فِي مَنَاكِبِهَا وَكُلُواْ مِن رِّزۡقِهِۦۖ وَإِلَيۡهِ ٱلنُّشُورُ
67:15.en: It is He who made the earth tame for you - so walk among its slopes and eat of His provision - and to Him is the resurrection

3:133.ar: ۞وَسَارِعُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ مَغۡفِرَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرۡضُهَا ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ أُعِدَّتۡ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ
3:133.en: And hasten to forgiveness from your Lord and a garden as wide as the heavens and earth, prepared for the righteous

57:21.ar: سَابِقُوٓاْ إِلَىٰ مَغۡفِرَةࣲ مِّن رَّبِّكُمۡ وَجَنَّةٍ عَرۡضُهَا كَعَرۡضِ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ أُعِدَّتۡ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ بِٱللَّهِ وَرُسُلِهِۦۚ ذَٰلِكَ فَضۡلُ ٱللَّهِ يُؤۡتِيهِ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَٱللَّهُ ذُو ٱلۡفَضۡلِ ٱلۡعَظِيمِ
57:21.en: Race toward forgiveness from your Lord and a Garden whose width is like the width of the heavens and earth, prepared for those who believed in Allah and His messengers. That is the bounty of Allah which He gives to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty

3:135.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ إِذَا فَعَلُواْ فَٰحِشَةً أَوۡ ظَلَمُوٓاْ أَنفُسَهُمۡ ذَكَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ فَٱسۡتَغۡفَرُواْ لِذُنُوبِهِمۡ وَمَن يَغۡفِرُ ٱلذُّنُوبَ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ وَلَمۡ يُصِرُّواْ عَلَىٰ مَا فَعَلُواْ وَهُمۡ يَعۡلَمُونَ
3:135.en: And those who, when they commit an immorality or wrong themselves [by transgression], remember Allah and seek forgiveness for their sins - and who can forgive sins except Allah? - and [who] do not persist in what they have done while they know

51:50.ar: فَفِرُّوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۖ إِنِّي لَكُم مِّنۡهُ نَذِيرࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
51:50.en: So flee to Allah. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner

24:22.ar: وَلَا يَأۡتَلِ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡفَضۡلِ مِنكُمۡ وَٱلسَّعَةِ أَن يُؤۡتُوٓاْ أُوْلِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينَ وَٱلۡمُهَٰجِرِينَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِۖ وَلۡيَعۡفُواْ وَلۡيَصۡفَحُوٓاْۗ أَلَا تُحِبُّونَ أَن يَغۡفِرَ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡۚ وَٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
24:22.en: And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear not to give [aid] to their relatives and the needy and the emigrants for the cause of Allah, and let them pardon and overlook. Would you not like that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful

12:92.ar: قَالَ لَا تَثۡرِيبَ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلۡيَوۡمَۖ يَغۡفِرُ ٱللَّهُ لَكُمۡۖ وَهُوَ أَرۡحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
12:92.en: He said, "No blame will there be upon you today. Allah will forgive you; and He is the most merciful of the merciful

12:100.ar: وَرَفَعَ أَبَوَيۡهِ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِ وَخَرُّواْ لَهُۥ سُجَّدࣰ اۖ وَقَالَ يَٰٓأَبَتِ هَٰذَا تَأۡوِيلُ رُءۡيَٰيَ مِن قَبۡلُ قَدۡ جَعَلَهَا رَبِّي حَقࣰّ اۖ وَقَدۡ أَحۡسَنَ بِيٓ إِذۡ أَخۡرَجَنِي مِنَ ٱلسِّجۡنِ وَجَآءَ بِكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡبَدۡوِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ أَن نَّزَغَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ بَيۡنِي وَبَيۡنَ إِخۡوَتِيٓۚ إِنَّ رَبِّي لَطِيفࣱ لِّمَا يَشَآءُۚ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
12:100.en: And he raised his parents upon the throne, and they bowed to him in prostration. And he said, "O my father, this is the explanation of my vision of before. My Lord has made it reality. And He was certainly good to me when He took me out of prison and brought you [here] from bedouin life after Satan had induced [estrangement] between me and my brothers. Indeed, my Lord is Subtle in what He wills. Indeed, it is He who is the Knowing, the Wise

66:8.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ تُوبُوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ تَوۡبَةࣰ نَّصُوحًا عَسَىٰ رَبُّكُمۡ أَن يُكَفِّرَ عَنكُمۡ سَيِّـَٔاتِكُمۡ وَيُدۡخِلَكُمۡ جَنَّٰتࣲ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهَا ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُ يَوۡمَ لَا يُخۡزِي ٱللَّهُ ٱلنَّبِيَّ وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ مَعَهُۥۖ نُورُهُمۡ يَسۡعَىٰ بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَبِأَيۡمَٰنِهِمۡ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَآ أَتۡمِمۡ لَنَا نُورَنَا وَٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَآۖ إِنَّكَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
66:8.en: O you who have believed, repent to Allah with sincere repentance. Perhaps your Lord will remove from you your misdeeds and admit you into gardens beneath which rivers flow [on] the Day when Allah will not disgrace the Prophet and those who believed with him. Their light will proceed before them and on their right; they will say, "Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us. Indeed, You are over all things competent

42:25.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي يَقۡبَلُ ٱلتَّوۡبَةَ عَنۡ عِبَادِهِۦ وَيَعۡفُواْ عَنِ ٱلسَّيِّـَٔاتِ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا تَفۡعَلُونَ
42:25.en: And it is He who accepts repentance from his servants and pardons misdeeds, and He knows what you do

25:68.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَدۡعُونَ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَ وَلَا يَقۡتُلُونَ ٱلنَّفۡسَ ٱلَّتِي حَرَّمَ ٱللَّهُ إِلَّا بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَلَا يَزۡنُونَۚ وَمَن يَفۡعَلۡ ذَٰلِكَ يَلۡقَ أَثَامࣰ ا
25:68.en: And those who do not invoke with Allah another deity or kill the soul which Allah has forbidden [to be killed], except by right, and do not commit unlawful sexual intercourse. And whoever should do that will meet a penalty

25:69.ar: يُضَٰعَفۡ لَهُ ٱلۡعَذَابُ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَيَخۡلُدۡ فِيهِۦ مُهَانًا
25:69.en: Multiplied for him is the punishment on the Day of Resurrection, and he will abide therein humiliated

25:70.ar: إِلَّا مَن تَابَ وَءَامَنَ وَعَمِلَ عَمَلࣰ ا صَٰلِحࣰ ا فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ يُبَدِّلُ ٱللَّهُ سَيِّـَٔاتِهِمۡ حَسَنَٰتࣲۗ وَكَانَ ٱللَّهُ غَفُورࣰ ا رَّحِيمࣰ ا
25:70.en: Except for those who repent, believe and do righteous work. For them Allah will replace their evil deeds with good. And ever is Allah Forgiving and Merciful

1hBPaO-AKfI.title: Ramadan 2026, Night 27: Tawbah and Forgiveness
1hBPaO-AKfI.one_line: Using the last nights to seek forgiveness: Allah's names of forgiveness, forgiving others like Abu Bakr and Yusuf, and the conditions of sincere tawbah.
1hBPaO-AKfI.summary: The speaker starts from Ramadan being a counted number of days that pass quickly, like life itself, and the story of two companions where the one who lived a year longer, fasting and praying more, entered paradise first. The last nights are like a treasure room open for thirty minutes, and forgiveness is its greatest treasure, since the one who reaches Ramadan unforgiven is warned and Laylat al-Qadr can equal a lifetime. He distinguishes istighfar from tawbah: major or repeated sins need regret and a plan to change. He explains Al-Ghafur and Al-Ghaffar, from a root meaning to cover, and Allah's concealment of our sins; every human errs, and the best are those who keep returning, as a child gets back on the bike. The Quran tells us to walk for provision but to race toward forgiveness and flee to Allah. Forgiving others is a path to being forgiven, as with Abu Bakr and Mistah and Yusuf, who forgave his brothers without reminding them. Tawbah is returning to the path like a rerouting map, and its conditions are stopping the sin, regret, resolving not to return, and repairing harm, after which Allah turns bad deeds into good.

outline.heading: Opening
A counted number of days
outline.gist: Ramadan passes as quickly as life does; with three nights left, ask whether you used the time well.

outline.heading: The companion who lived one more year
outline.gist: Of two men who accepted Islam together, the one who outlived the martyr by a year entered paradise first, because of the extra Ramadan and prayers.

outline.heading: A treasure room open for thirty minutes
outline.gist: Would you spend limited access to a room of treasure scrolling Instagram, or seek the most valuable thing in it?

outline.heading: Forgiveness, the greatest treasure
outline.gist: The Prophet said ameen on the minbar to Jibril's dua against one who reaches Ramadan and is not forgiven.

outline.heading: Laylat al-Qadr: one moment worth a lifetime
outline.gist: A single act of high-quality worship can earn the reward of a thousand months; this may be our last chance.

outline.heading: Istighfar versus tawbah
outline.gist: For major or repeated sins asking forgiveness is not enough; one must regret the sin and plan to rectify it.

outline.heading: Maghfirah means covering
outline.gist: The root of Allah's names of forgiveness means to cover; His concealment of our sins is a mercy, or we could not face one another.

outline.heading: Al-Ghafur and Al-Ghaffar
outline.gist: Al-Ghafur forgives every kind of sin, great and small; Al-Ghaffar, in an intensive form, keeps forgiving time after time.

outline.heading: Every human errs; get back on the bike
outline.gist: The best sinners are those who repent; like a child who falls off a bike, we keep returning to Allah, who forgives sins that reach the sky.

outline.heading: Everything forgiven except shirk
outline.gist: Allah forgives all sins below associating partners with Him for whom He wills.

outline.heading: Walk for provision, race for forgiveness
outline.gist: The Quran says to walk the earth for provision but to hasten and compete for forgiveness.

outline.heading: Remember Allah and flee to Him
outline.gist: Those who wrong themselves remember Allah and seek forgiveness; the believer flees back to Him.

outline.heading: Forgive to be forgiven: Abu Bakr and Mistah
outline.gist: After the slander against Aisha, Abu Bakr swore to stop supporting Mistah, and was told: do you not love that Allah forgive you?

outline.heading: Yusuf forgives his brothers
outline.gist: Thrown in a well, enslaved and imprisoned, Yusuf told his brothers there is no blame today and later mentioned only the prison, blaming Shaytan for the rift.

outline.heading: Forgiveness without reminding
outline.gist: Real forgiveness does not keep count, humiliate or remind the person; ask who in your life you can forgive.

outline.heading: Tawbah means returning to the route
outline.gist: Sincere repentance is like a map app rerouting you to the original path after a wrong turn; At-Tawwab keeps accepting the return.

outline.heading: A clean slate
outline.gist: Allah accepts repentance from His servants and pardons their bad deeds.

outline.heading: Come walking and He comes running
outline.gist: In a hadith qudsi, whoever meets Allah with an earth-full of sins, without shirk, is met with as much forgiveness.

outline.heading: First condition: stop the sin
outline.gist: You cannot claim to return to Allah while still committing the sin.

outline.heading: Second condition: genuine regret
outline.gist: Without believing the act is wrong, as with someone who does not think smoking is haram, behaviour never changes.

outline.heading: Third condition: a plan not to return
outline.gist: Identify what pulls you back, such as friends or environment, and plan how to leave it.

outline.heading: Fourth condition: repair the harm
outline.gist: Those who repent, believe and do righteous deeds have their bad deeds replaced with good ones.

outline.heading: Transformed in the last nights
outline.gist: He asks that we leave Ramadan forgiven, transformed and connected to the Quran.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance and returning to Allah
themes.note: Tawbah is returning to the path; for major or repeated sins it requires stopping, regret, a plan and repairing harm.

themes.label: The Names and Attributes of Allah
themes.note: Al-Ghafur, Al-Ghaffar and At-Tawwab describe a Lord who covers sins and keeps forgiving.

themes.label: Mercy, forgiveness and pardoning people
themes.note: Forgiving others, without reminding or humiliating them, is a way to earn Allah's forgiveness.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: The last nights are a limited treasure room whose greatest prize is forgiveness.

themes.label: Time, opportunity and seizing the moment
themes.note: One extra year of fasting and prayer raised a companion above a martyr; time slips by like Ramadan.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Yusuf's forgiveness of his brothers is the model of forgiving without reproach.

quran.point: Fasting is for a counted number of days.
Laylat al-Qadr is better than a thousand months.
By time, mankind is in loss.
Allah does not forgive shirk but forgives anything less for whom He wills.
After prayer disperse in the land and seek Allah's bounty.
Walk through the earth and eat of His provision: walking for rizq.
Hasten to forgiveness from your Lord.
Race toward forgiveness from your Lord.
Those who commit an indecency or wrong themselves remember Allah and seek forgiveness.
So flee to Allah.
Let them pardon and overlook; do you not love that Allah forgive you?
No blame on you today.
Yusuf mentions being freed from prison and blames Shaytan for the rift, not his brothers.
Turn to Allah in sincere repentance.
He accepts repentance from His servants and pardons bad deeds.
Except whoever repents, believes and does righteous deeds: Allah replaces their bad deeds with good.

hadith.gist: Talhah dreamt that of two companions, the one who died a year after the martyr entered paradise first; the Prophet explained he had fasted another Ramadan and prayed so many more prayers.
The Prophet said ameen on the minbar when Jibril prayed against the one who reaches Ramadan and is not forgiven.
Allah looked at the people of Badr and said do as you wish, for I have forgiven you.
Every child of Adam errs, and the best of those who err are those who repent.
O son of Adam, as long as you call on Me and hope in Me I will forgive you, even if your sins reach the clouds of the sky.
Whoever comes to Allah walking, He comes to him running; whoever meets Him with an earth-full of sins without shirk, He meets with as much forgiveness.

maxims: Walk for provision, race for forgiveness
Forgiveness that comes with counting is not forgiveness

stories.who: Two companions, one martyred and one who lived a year longer
stories.point: An extra Ramadan of fasting and prayer can outweigh martyrdom; value the time left.

stories.who: Abu Bakr and Mistah after the slander of Aisha
stories.point: Forgiving those who wronged you is how you seek Allah's forgiveness.

stories.who: Yusuf and his brothers
stories.point: True forgiveness never reminds or humiliates the one forgiven.

takeaways: Treat the remaining nights as limited access to a treasure and seek forgiveness above all.
For repeated or major sins, stop, regret, plan to avoid the triggers, and repair any harm done.
Forgive someone who wronged you, and do not remind them of it afterwards.
Keep returning to Allah after every fall instead of giving up.

51:2.en: And those [clouds] carrying a load [of water]

51:5.en: Indeed, what you are promised is true

51:6.en: And indeed, the recompense is to occur

51:8.en: Indeed, you are in differing speech

51:9.en: Deluded away from the Qur'an is he who is deluded

51:11.en: Who are within a flood [of confusion] and heedless

51:12.en: They ask, "When is the Day of Recompense

51:13.en: [It is] the Day they will be tormented over the Fire

51:14.ar: ذُوقُواْ فِتۡنَتَكُمۡ هَٰذَا ٱلَّذِي كُنتُم بِهِۦ تَسۡتَعۡجِلُونَ
51:14.en: [And will be told], "Taste your torment. This is that for which you were impatient

51:15.en: Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and springs

51:16.ar: ءَاخِذِينَ مَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمۡ رَبُّهُمۡۚ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ قَبۡلَ ذَٰلِكَ مُحۡسِنِينَ
51:16.en: Accepting what their Lord has given them. Indeed, they were before that doers of good

51:17.ar: كَانُواْ قَلِيلࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلَّيۡلِ مَا يَهۡجَعُونَ
51:17.en: They used to sleep but little of the night

51:18.en: And in the hours before dawn they would ask forgiveness

51:19.en: And from their properties was [given] the right of the [needy] petitioner and the deprived

51:20.en: And on the earth are signs for the certain [in faith]

51:21.en: And in yourselves. Then will you not see

51:22.en: And in the heaven is your provision and whatever you are promised

51:23.ar: فَوَرَبِّ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ إِنَّهُۥ لَحَقࣱّ مِّثۡلَ مَآ أَنَّكُمۡ تَنطِقُونَ
51:23.en: Then by the Lord of the heaven and earth, indeed, it is truth - just as [sure as] it is that you are speaking

51:24.ar: هَلۡ أَتَىٰكَ حَدِيثُ ضَيۡفِ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ ٱلۡمُكۡرَمِينَ
51:24.en: Has there reached you the story of the honored guests of Abraham

51:25.ar: إِذۡ دَخَلُواْ عَلَيۡهِ فَقَالُواْ سَلَٰمࣰ اۖ قَالَ سَلَٰمࣱ قَوۡمࣱ مُّنكَرُونَ
51:25.en: When they entered upon him and said, "[We greet you with] peace." He answered, "[And upon you] peace, [you are] a people unknown

51:26.ar: فَرَاغَ إِلَىٰٓ أَهۡلِهِۦ فَجَآءَ بِعِجۡلࣲ سَمِينࣲ‏
51:26.en: Then he went to his family and came with a fat [roasted] calf

51:27.en: And placed it near them; he said, "Will you not eat

51:28.ar: فَأَوۡجَسَ مِنۡهُمۡ خِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُواْ لَا تَخَفۡۖ وَبَشَّرُوهُ بِغُلَٰمٍ عَلِيمࣲ‏
51:28.en: And he felt from them apprehension. They said, "Fear not," and gave him good tidings of a learned boy

51:29.ar: فَأَقۡبَلَتِ ٱمۡرَأَتُهُۥ فِي صَرَّةࣲ فَصَكَّتۡ وَجۡهَهَا وَقَالَتۡ عَجُوزٌ عَقِيمࣱ‏
51:29.en: And his wife approached with a cry [of alarm] and struck her face and said, "[I am] a barren old woman

51:30.ar: قَالُواْ كَذَٰلِكِ قَالَ رَبُّكِۖ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
51:30.en: They said, "Thus has said your Lord; indeed, He is the Wise, the Knowing

51:31.en: [Abraham] said, "Then what is your business [here], O messengers

51:32.ar: قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّآ أُرۡسِلۡنَآ إِلَىٰ قَوۡمࣲ مُّجۡرِمِينَ
51:32.en: They said, "Indeed, we have been sent to a people of criminals

51:33.en: To send down upon them stones of clay

51:34.en: Marked in the presence of your Lord for the transgressors

51:35.ar: فَأَخۡرَجۡنَا مَن كَانَ فِيهَا مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ
51:35.en: So We brought out whoever was in the cities of the believers

51:36.ar: فَمَا وَجَدۡنَا فِيهَا غَيۡرَ بَيۡتࣲ مِّنَ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ
51:36.en: And We found not within them other than a [single] house of Muslims

51:37.ar: وَتَرَكۡنَا فِيهَآ ءَايَةࣰ لِّلَّذِينَ يَخَافُونَ ٱلۡعَذَابَ ٱلۡأَلِيمَ
51:37.en: And We left therein a sign for those who fear the painful punishment

51:38.ar: وَفِي مُوسَىٰٓ إِذۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَٰهُ إِلَىٰ فِرۡعَوۡنَ بِسُلۡطَٰنࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
51:38.en: And in Moses [was a sign], when We sent him to Pharaoh with clear authority

51:39.ar: فَتَوَلَّىٰ بِرُكۡنِهِۦ وَقَالَ سَٰحِرٌ أَوۡ مَجۡنُونࣱ‏
51:39.en: But he turned away with his supporters and said," A magician or a madman

51:40.ar: فَأَخَذۡنَٰهُ وَجُنُودَهُۥ فَنَبَذۡنَٰهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡيَمِّ وَهُوَ مُلِيمࣱ‏
51:40.en: So We took him and his soldiers and cast them into the sea, and he was blameworthy

51:41.ar: وَفِي عَادٍ إِذۡ أَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمُ ٱلرِّيحَ ٱلۡعَقِيمَ
51:41.en: And in 'Aad [was a sign], when We sent against them the barren wind

51:42.ar: مَا تَذَرُ مِن شَيۡءٍ أَتَتۡ عَلَيۡهِ إِلَّا جَعَلَتۡهُ كَٱلرَّمِيمِ
51:42.en: It left nothing of what it came upon but that it made it like disintegrated ruins

51:43.ar: وَفِي ثَمُودَ إِذۡ قِيلَ لَهُمۡ تَمَتَّعُواْ حَتَّىٰ حِينࣲ‏
51:43.en: And in Thamud, when it was said to them, "Enjoy yourselves for a time

51:44.ar: فَعَتَوۡاْ عَنۡ أَمۡرِ رَبِّهِمۡ فَأَخَذَتۡهُمُ ٱلصَّٰعِقَةُ وَهُمۡ يَنظُرُونَ
51:44.en: But they were insolent toward the command of their Lord, so the thunderbolt seized them while they were looking on

51:45.ar: فَمَا ٱسۡتَطَٰعُواْ مِن قِيَامࣲ وَمَا كَانُواْ مُنتَصِرِينَ
51:45.en: And they were unable to arise, nor could they defend themselves

51:46.ar: وَقَوۡمَ نُوحࣲ مِّن قَبۡلُۖ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ قَوۡمࣰ ا فَٰسِقِينَ
51:46.en: And [We destroyed] the people of Noah before; indeed, they were a people defiantly disobedient

51:47.en: And the heaven We constructed with strength, and indeed, We are [its] expander

51:48.en: And the earth We have spread out, and excellent is the preparer

51:49.ar: وَمِن كُلِّ شَيۡءٍ خَلَقۡنَا زَوۡجَيۡنِ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَذَكَّرُونَ
51:49.en: And of all things We created two mates; perhaps you will remember

51:50.ar: فَفِرُّوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِۖ إِنِّي لَكُم مِّنۡهُ نَذِيرࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
51:50.en: So flee to Allah. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner

51:51.ar: وَلَا تَجۡعَلُواْ مَعَ ٱللَّهِ إِلَٰهًا ءَاخَرَۖ إِنِّي لَكُم مِّنۡهُ نَذِيرࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
51:51.en: And do not make [as equal] with Allah another deity. Indeed, I am to you from Him a clear warner

51:52.ar: كَذَٰلِكَ مَآ أَتَى ٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِهِم مِّن رَّسُولٍ إِلَّا قَالُواْ سَاحِرٌ أَوۡ مَجۡنُونٌ
51:52.en: Similarly, there came not to those before them any messenger except that they said, "A magician or a madman

51:53.ar: أَتَوَاصَوۡاْ بِهِۦۚ بَلۡ هُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ طَاغُونَ
51:53.en: Did they suggest it to them? Rather, they [themselves] are a transgressing people

51:54.en: So leave them, [O Muhammad], for you are not to be blamed

51:55.en: And remind, for indeed, the reminder benefits the believers

51:56.ar: وَمَا خَلَقۡتُ ٱلۡجِنَّ وَٱلۡإِنسَ إِلَّا لِيَعۡبُدُونِ
51:56.en: And I did not create the jinn and mankind except to worship Me

51:57.ar: مَآ أُرِيدُ مِنۡهُم مِّن رِّزۡقࣲ وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَن يُطۡعِمُونِ
51:57.en: I do not want from them any provision, nor do I want them to feed Me

51:58.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ هُوَ ٱلرَّزَّاقُ ذُو ٱلۡقُوَّةِ ٱلۡمَتِينُ
51:58.en: Indeed, it is Allah who is the [continual] Provider, the firm possessor of strength

51:59.ar: فَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ ذَنُوبࣰ ا مِّثۡلَ ذَنُوبِ أَصۡحَٰبِهِمۡ فَلَا يَسۡتَعۡجِلُونِ
51:59.en: And indeed, for those who have wronged is a portion [of punishment] like the portion of their predecessors, so let them not impatiently urge Me

51:60.ar: فَوَيۡلࣱ لِّلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِن يَوۡمِهِمُ ٱلَّذِي يُوعَدُونَ
51:60.en: And woe to those who have disbelieved from their Day which they are promised

52:7.en: Indeed, the punishment of your Lord will occur

52:8.en: Of it there is no preventer

52:9.en: On the Day the heaven will sway with circular motion

52:10.en: And the mountains will pass on, departing

52:11.en: Then woe, that Day, to the deniers

52:12.en: Who are in [empty] discourse amusing themselves

52:13.ar: يَوۡمَ يُدَعُّونَ إِلَىٰ نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ دَعًّا
52:13.en: The Day they are thrust toward the fire of Hell with a [violent] thrust, [its angels will say]

52:14.ar: هَٰذِهِ ٱلنَّارُ ٱلَّتِي كُنتُم بِهَا تُكَذِّبُونَ
52:14.en: This is the Fire which you used to deny

52:15.ar: أَفَسِحۡرٌ هَٰذَآ أَمۡ أَنتُمۡ لَا تُبۡصِرُونَ
52:15.en: Then is this magic, or do you not see

52:16.ar: ٱصۡلَوۡهَا فَٱصۡبِرُوٓاْ أَوۡ لَا تَصۡبِرُواْ سَوَآءٌ عَلَيۡكُمۡۖ إِنَّمَا تُجۡزَوۡنَ مَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
52:16.en: [Enter to] burn therein; then be patient or impatient - it is all the same for you. You are only being recompensed [for] what you used to do

52:17.en: Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and pleasure

52:18.ar: فَٰكِهِينَ بِمَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمۡ رَبُّهُمۡ وَوَقَىٰهُمۡ رَبُّهُمۡ عَذَابَ ٱلۡجَحِيمِ
52:18.en: Enjoying what their Lord has given them, and their Lord protected them from the punishment of Hellfire

52:19.ar: كُلُواْ وَٱشۡرَبُواْ هَنِيٓـَٔۢا بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ
52:19.en: [They will be told], "Eat and drink in satisfaction for what you used to do

52:20.ar: مُتَّكِـِٔينَ عَلَىٰ سُرُرࣲ مَّصۡفُوفَةࣲۖ وَزَوَّجۡنَٰهُم بِحُورٍ عِينࣲ‏
52:20.en: They will be reclining on thrones lined up, and We will marry them to fair women with large, [beautiful] eyes

52:21.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَٱتَّبَعَتۡهُمۡ ذُرِّيَّتُهُم بِإِيمَٰنٍ أَلۡحَقۡنَا بِهِمۡ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمۡ وَمَآ أَلَتۡنَٰهُم مِّنۡ عَمَلِهِم مِّن شَيۡءࣲۚ كُلُّ ٱمۡرِيِٕۭ بِمَا كَسَبَ رَهِينࣱ‏
52:21.en: And those who believed and whose descendants followed them in faith - We will join with them their descendants, and We will not deprive them of anything of their deeds. Every person, for what he earned, is retained

52:22.en: And We will provide them with fruit and meat from whatever they desire

52:23.ar: يَتَنَٰزَعُونَ فِيهَا كَأۡسࣰ ا لَّا لَغۡوࣱ فِيهَا وَلَا تَأۡثِيمࣱ‏
52:23.en: They will exchange with one another a cup [of wine] wherein [results] no ill speech or commission of sin

52:24.ar: ۞وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيۡهِمۡ غِلۡمَانࣱ لَّهُمۡ كَأَنَّهُمۡ لُؤۡلُؤࣱ مَّكۡنُونࣱ‏
52:24.en: There will circulate among them [servant] boys [especially] for them, as if they were pearls well-protected

52:25.en: And they will approach one another, inquiring of each other

52:26.ar: قَالُوٓاْ إِنَّا كُنَّا قَبۡلُ فِيٓ أَهۡلِنَا مُشۡفِقِينَ
52:26.en: They will say, "Indeed, we were previously among our people fearful [of displeasing Allah]

52:27.ar: فَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡنَا وَوَقَىٰنَا عَذَابَ ٱلسَّمُومِ
52:27.en: So Allah conferred favor upon us and protected us from the punishment of the Scorching Fire

52:28.ar: إِنَّا كُنَّا مِن قَبۡلُ نَدۡعُوهُۖ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلۡبَرُّ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
52:28.en: Indeed, we used to supplicate Him before. Indeed, it is He who is the Beneficent, the Merciful

52:29.ar: فَذَكِّرۡ فَمَآ أَنتَ بِنِعۡمَتِ رَبِّكَ بِكَاهِنࣲ وَلَا مَجۡنُونٍ
52:29.en: So remind [O Muhammad], for you are not, by the favor of your Lord, a soothsayer or a madman

52:30.ar: أَمۡ يَقُولُونَ شَاعِرࣱ نَّتَرَبَّصُ بِهِۦ رَيۡبَ ٱلۡمَنُونِ
52:30.en: Or do they say [of you], "A poet for whom we await a misfortune of time

52:31.ar: قُلۡ تَرَبَّصُواْ فَإِنِّي مَعَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡمُتَرَبِّصِينَ
52:31.en: Say, "Wait, for indeed I am, with you, among the waiters

52:32.ar: أَمۡ تَأۡمُرُهُمۡ أَحۡلَٰمُهُم بِهَٰذَآۚ أَمۡ هُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ طَاغُونَ
52:32.en: Or do their minds command them to [say] this, or are they a transgressing people

52:33.ar: أَمۡ يَقُولُونَ تَقَوَّلَهُۥۚ بَل لَّا يُؤۡمِنُونَ
52:33.en: Or do they say, "He has made it up"? Rather, they do not believe

52:34.ar: فَلۡيَأۡتُواْ بِحَدِيثࣲ مِّثۡلِهِۦٓ إِن كَانُواْ صَٰدِقِينَ
52:34.en: Then let them produce a statement like it, if they should be truthful

52:35.ar: أَمۡ خُلِقُواْ مِنۡ غَيۡرِ شَيۡءٍ أَمۡ هُمُ ٱلۡخَٰلِقُونَ
52:35.en: Or were they created by nothing, or were they the creators [of themselves]

52:36.ar: أَمۡ خَلَقُواْ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَۚ بَل لَّا يُوقِنُونَ
52:36.en: Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they are not certain

52:37.ar: أَمۡ عِندَهُمۡ خَزَآئِنُ رَبِّكَ أَمۡ هُمُ ٱلۡمُصَۜيۡطِرُونَ
52:37.en: Or have they the depositories [containing the provision] of your Lord? Or are they the controllers [of them]

52:38.ar: أَمۡ لَهُمۡ سُلَّمࣱ يَسۡتَمِعُونَ فِيهِۖ فَلۡيَأۡتِ مُسۡتَمِعُهُم بِسُلۡطَٰنࣲ مُّبِينٍ
52:38.en: Or have they a stairway [into the heaven] upon which they listen? Then let their listener produce a clear authority

52:39.en: Or has He daughters while you have sons

52:40.ar: أَمۡ تَسۡـَٔلُهُمۡ أَجۡرࣰ ا فَهُم مِّن مَّغۡرَمࣲ مُّثۡقَلُونَ
52:40.en: Or do you, [O Muhammad], ask of them a payment, so they are by debt burdened down

52:41.en: Or have they [knowledge of] the unseen, so they write [it] down

52:42.ar: أَمۡ يُرِيدُونَ كَيۡدࣰ اۖ فَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ هُمُ ٱلۡمَكِيدُونَ
52:42.en: Or do they intend a plan? But those who disbelieve - they are the object of a plan

52:43.ar: أَمۡ لَهُمۡ إِلَٰهٌ غَيۡرُ ٱللَّهِۚ سُبۡحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
52:43.en: Or have they a deity other than Allah? Exalted is Allah above whatever they associate with Him

52:44.ar: وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ كِسۡفࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ سَاقِطࣰ ا يَقُولُواْ سَحَابࣱ مَّرۡكُومࣱ‏
52:44.en: And if they were to see a fragment from the sky falling, they would say, "[It is merely] clouds heaped up

52:45.ar: فَذَرۡهُمۡ حَتَّىٰ يُلَٰقُواْ يَوۡمَهُمُ ٱلَّذِي فِيهِ يُصۡعَقُونَ
52:45.en: So leave them until they meet their Day in which they will be struck insensible

52:46.ar: يَوۡمَ لَا يُغۡنِي عَنۡهُمۡ كَيۡدُهُمۡ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا وَلَا هُمۡ يُنصَرُونَ
52:46.en: The Day their plan will not avail them at all, nor will they be helped

52:47.ar: وَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُواْ عَذَابࣰ ا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكۡثَرَهُمۡ لَا يَعۡلَمُونَ
52:47.en: And indeed, for those who have wronged is a punishment before that, but most of them do not know

52:48.ar: وَٱصۡبِرۡ لِحُكۡمِ رَبِّكَ فَإِنَّكَ بِأَعۡيُنِنَاۖ وَسَبِّحۡ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ
52:48.en: And be patient, [O Muhammad], for the decision of your Lord, for indeed, you are in Our eyes. And exalt [Allah] with praise of your Lord when you arise

52:49.en: And in a part of the night exalt Him and after [the setting of] the stars

53:1.en: By the star when it descends

53:2.en: Your companion [Muhammad] has not strayed, nor has he erred

53:3.en: Nor does he speak from [his own] inclination

53:4.en: It is not but a revelation revealed

53:5.en: Taught to him by one intense in strength

53:6.en: One of soundness. And he rose to [his] true form

53:7.en: While he was in the higher [part of the] horizon

53:9.en: And was at a distance of two bow lengths or nearer

53:10.en: And he revealed to His Servant what he revealed

53:11.en: The heart did not lie [about] what it saw

53:12.en: So will you dispute with him over what he saw

53:13.en: And he certainly saw him in another descent

53:14.en: At the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary

53:15.en: Near it is the Garden of Refuge

53:16.en: When there covered the Lote Tree that which covered [it]

53:17.en: The sight [of the Prophet] did not swerve, nor did it transgress [its limit]

53:18.ar: لَقَدۡ رَأَىٰ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِ رَبِّهِ ٱلۡكُبۡرَىٰٓ
53:18.en: He certainly saw of the greatest signs of his Lord

53:19.en: So have you considered al-Lat and al-'Uzza

53:20.en: And Manat, the third - the other one

53:21.en: Is the male for you and for Him the female

53:22.en: That, then, is an unjust division

53:23.ar: إِنۡ هِيَ إِلَّآ أَسۡمَآءࣱ سَمَّيۡتُمُوهَآ أَنتُمۡ وَءَابَآؤُكُم مَّآ أَنزَلَ ٱللَّهُ بِهَا مِن سُلۡطَٰنٍۚ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّ وَمَا تَهۡوَى ٱلۡأَنفُسُۖ وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَهُم مِّن رَّبِّهِمُ ٱلۡهُدَىٰٓ
53:23.en: They are not but [mere] names you have named them - you and your forefathers - for which Allah has sent down no authority. They follow not except assumption and what [their] souls desire, and there has already come to them from their Lord guidance

53:24.en: Or is there for man whatever he wishes

53:25.en: Rather, to Allah belongs the Hereafter and the first [life]

53:26.ar: ۞وَكَم مِّن مَّلَكࣲ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ لَا تُغۡنِي شَفَٰعَتُهُمۡ شَيۡـًٔا إِلَّا مِنۢ بَعۡدِ أَن يَأۡذَنَ ٱللَّهُ لِمَن يَشَآءُ وَيَرۡضَىٰٓ
53:26.en: And how many angels there are in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all except [only] after Allah has permitted [it] to whom He wills and approves

53:27.ar: إِنَّ ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يُؤۡمِنُونَ بِٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ لَيُسَمُّونَ ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةَ تَسۡمِيَةَ ٱلۡأُنثَىٰ
53:27.en: Indeed, those who do not believe in the Hereafter name the angels female names

53:28.ar: وَمَا لَهُم بِهِۦ مِنۡ عِلۡمٍۖ إِن يَتَّبِعُونَ إِلَّا ٱلظَّنَّۖ وَإِنَّ ٱلظَّنَّ لَا يُغۡنِي مِنَ ٱلۡحَقِّ شَيۡـࣰٔ ا
53:28.en: And they have thereof no knowledge. They follow not except assumption, and indeed, assumption avails not against the truth at all

53:29.ar: فَأَعۡرِضۡ عَن مَّن تَوَلَّىٰ عَن ذِكۡرِنَا وَلَمۡ يُرِدۡ إِلَّا ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا
53:29.en: So turn away from whoever turns his back on Our message and desires not except the worldly life

53:30.ar: ذَٰلِكَ مَبۡلَغُهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡعِلۡمِۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَن ضَلَّ عَن سَبِيلِهِۦ وَهُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَنِ ٱهۡتَدَىٰ
53:30.en: That is their sum of knowledge. Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who strays from His way, and He is most knowing of who is guided

53:31.ar: وَلِلَّهِ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ لِيَجۡزِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَسَٰٓـُٔواْ بِمَا عَمِلُواْ وَيَجۡزِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَحۡسَنُواْ بِٱلۡحُسۡنَى
53:31.en: And to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is in the earth - that He may recompense those who do evil with [the penalty of] what they have done and recompense those who do good with the best [reward]

53:32.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَجۡتَنِبُونَ كَبَٰٓئِرَ ٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡفَوَٰحِشَ إِلَّا ٱللَّمَمَۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ وَٰسِعُ ٱلۡمَغۡفِرَةِۚ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِكُمۡ إِذۡ أَنشَأَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَإِذۡ أَنتُمۡ أَجِنَّةࣱ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمۡۖ فَلَا تُزَكُّوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡۖ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰٓ
53:32.en: Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, only [committing] slight ones. Indeed, your Lord is vast in forgiveness. He was most knowing of you when He produced you from the earth and when you were fetuses in the wombs of your mothers. So do not claim yourselves to be pure; He is most knowing of who fears Him

53:33.en: Have you seen the one who turned away

53:34.en: And gave a little and [then] refrained

53:35.en: Does he have knowledge of the unseen, so he sees

53:36.ar: أَمۡ لَمۡ يُنَبَّأۡ بِمَا فِي صُحُفِ مُوسَىٰ
53:36.en: Or has he not been informed of what was in the scriptures of Moses

53:38.en: That no bearer of burdens will bear the burden of another

53:39.ar: وَأَن لَّيۡسَ لِلۡإِنسَٰنِ إِلَّا مَا سَعَىٰ
53:39.en: And that there is not for man except that [good] for which he strives

53:40.en: And that his effort is going to be seen

53:41.en: Then he will be recompensed for it with the fullest recompense

53:42.en: And that to your Lord is the finality

53:43.en: And that it is He who makes [one] laugh and weep

53:44.en: And that it is He who causes death and gives life

53:45.en: And that He creates the two mates - the male and female

53:46.en: From a sperm-drop when it is emitted

53:47.en: And that [incumbent] upon Him is the next creation

53:48.en: And that it is He who enriches and suffices

53:49.en: And that it is He who is the Lord of Sirius

53:50.en: And that He destroyed the first [people of] 'Aad

53:51.en: And Thamud - and He did not spare [them]

53:52.ar: وَقَوۡمَ نُوحࣲ مِّن قَبۡلُۖ إِنَّهُمۡ كَانُواْ هُمۡ أَظۡلَمَ وَأَطۡغَىٰ
53:52.en: And the people of Noah before. Indeed, it was they who were [even] more unjust and oppressing

53:53.en: And the overturned towns He hurled down

53:54.en: And covered them by that which He covered

53:55.en: Then which of the favors of your Lord do you doubt

53:56.en: This [Prophet] is a warner like the former warners

53:58.ar: لَيۡسَ لَهَا مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ كَاشِفَةٌ
53:58.en: Of it, [from those] besides Allah, there is no remover

53:59.en: Then at this statement do you wonder

53:60.en: And you laugh and do not weep

54:1.en: The Hour has come near, and the moon has split [in two]

54:2.ar: وَإِن يَرَوۡاْ ءَايَةࣰ يُعۡرِضُواْ وَيَقُولُواْ سِحۡرࣱ مُّسۡتَمِرࣱّ‏
54:2.en: And if they see a miracle, they turn away and say, "Passing magic

54:3.ar: وَكَذَّبُواْ وَٱتَّبَعُوٓاْ أَهۡوَآءَهُمۡۚ وَكُلُّ أَمۡرࣲ مُّسۡتَقِرࣱّ‏
54:3.en: And they denied and followed their inclinations. But for every matter is a [time of] settlement

54:4.ar: وَلَقَدۡ جَآءَهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَنۢبَآءِ مَا فِيهِ مُزۡدَجَرٌ
54:4.en: And there has already come to them of information that in which there is deterrence

54:5.en: Extensive wisdom - but warning does not avail [them]

54:6.ar: فَتَوَلَّ عَنۡهُمۡۘ يَوۡمَ يَدۡعُ ٱلدَّاعِ إِلَىٰ شَيۡءࣲ نُّكُرٍ
54:6.en: So leave them, [O Muhammad]. The Day the Caller calls to something forbidding

54:7.ar: خُشَّعًا أَبۡصَٰرُهُمۡ يَخۡرُجُونَ مِنَ ٱلۡأَجۡدَاثِ كَأَنَّهُمۡ جَرَادࣱ مُّنتَشِرࣱ‏
54:7.en: Their eyes humbled, they will emerge from the graves as if they were locusts spreading

54:8.ar: مُّهۡطِعِينَ إِلَى ٱلدَّاعِۖ يَقُولُ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ هَٰذَا يَوۡمٌ عَسِرࣱ‏
54:8.en: Racing ahead toward the Caller. The disbelievers will say, "This is a difficult Day

54:9.ar: ۞كَذَّبَتۡ قَبۡلَهُمۡ قَوۡمُ نُوحࣲ فَكَذَّبُواْ عَبۡدَنَا وَقَالُواْ مَجۡنُونࣱ وَٱزۡدُجِرَ
54:9.en: The people of Noah denied before them, and they denied Our servant and said, "A madman," and he was repelled

54:10.en: So he invoked his Lord, "Indeed, I am overpowered, so help

54:11.en: Then We opened the gates of the heaven with rain pouring down

54:12.ar: وَفَجَّرۡنَا ٱلۡأَرۡضَ عُيُونࣰ ا فَٱلۡتَقَى ٱلۡمَآءُ عَلَىٰٓ أَمۡرࣲ قَدۡ قُدِرَ
54:12.en: And caused the earth to burst with springs, and the waters met for a matter already predestined

54:13.en: And We carried him on a [construction of] planks and nails

54:14.ar: تَجۡرِي بِأَعۡيُنِنَا جَزَآءࣰ لِّمَن كَانَ كُفِرَ
54:14.en: Sailing under Our observation as reward for he who had been denied

54:15.ar: وَلَقَد تَّرَكۡنَٰهَآ ءَايَةࣰ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرࣲ‏
54:15.en: And We left it as a sign, so is there any who will remember

54:16.en: And how [severe] were My punishment and warning

54:17.ar: وَلَقَدۡ يَسَّرۡنَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ لِلذِّكۡرِ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرࣲ‏
54:17.en: And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember

54:18.ar: كَذَّبَتۡ عَادࣱ فَكَيۡفَ كَانَ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ
54:18.en: Aad denied; and how [severe] were My punishment and warning

54:19.ar: إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ رِيحࣰ ا صَرۡصَرࣰ ا فِي يَوۡمِ نَحۡسࣲ مُّسۡتَمِرࣲّ‏
54:19.en: Indeed, We sent upon them a screaming wind on a day of continuous misfortune

54:20.ar: تَنزِعُ ٱلنَّاسَ كَأَنَّهُمۡ أَعۡجَازُ نَخۡلࣲ مُّنقَعِرࣲ‏
54:20.en: Extracting the people as if they were trunks of palm trees uprooted

54:21.en: And how [severe] were My punishment and warning

54:22.ar: وَلَقَدۡ يَسَّرۡنَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ لِلذِّكۡرِ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرࣲ‏
54:22.en: And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember

54:24.ar: فَقَالُوٓاْ أَبَشَرࣰ ا مِّنَّا وَٰحِدࣰ ا نَّتَّبِعُهُۥٓ إِنَّآ إِذࣰ ا لَّفِي ضَلَٰلࣲ وَسُعُرٍ
54:24.en: And said, "Is it one human being among us that we should follow? Indeed, we would then be in error and madness

54:25.ar: أَءُلۡقِيَ ٱلذِّكۡرُ عَلَيۡهِ مِنۢ بَيۡنِنَا بَلۡ هُوَ كَذَّابٌ أَشِرࣱ‏
54:25.en: Has the message been sent down upon him from among us? Rather, he is an insolent liar

54:26.ar: سَيَعۡلَمُونَ غَدࣰ ا مَّنِ ٱلۡكَذَّابُ ٱلۡأَشِرُ
54:26.en: They will know tomorrow who is the insolent liar

54:27.ar: إِنَّا مُرۡسِلُواْ ٱلنَّاقَةِ فِتۡنَةࣰ لَّهُمۡ فَٱرۡتَقِبۡهُمۡ وَٱصۡطَبِرۡ
54:27.en: Indeed, We are sending the she-camel as trial for them, so watch them and be patient

54:28.ar: وَنَبِّئۡهُمۡ أَنَّ ٱلۡمَآءَ قِسۡمَةُۢ بَيۡنَهُمۡۖ كُلُّ شِرۡبࣲ مُّحۡتَضَرࣱ‏
54:28.en: And inform them that the water is shared between them, each [day of] drink attended [by turn]

54:29.en: But they called their companion, and he dared and hamstrung [her]

54:30.en: And how [severe] were My punishment and warning

54:31.ar: إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ صَيۡحَةࣰ وَٰحِدَةࣰ فَكَانُواْ كَهَشِيمِ ٱلۡمُحۡتَظِرِ
54:31.en: Indeed, We sent upon them one blast from the sky, and they became like the dry twig fragments of an [animal] pen

54:32.ar: وَلَقَدۡ يَسَّرۡنَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ لِلذِّكۡرِ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرࣲ‏
54:32.en: And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember

54:33.en: The people of Lot denied the warning

54:34.ar: إِنَّآ أَرۡسَلۡنَا عَلَيۡهِمۡ حَاصِبًا إِلَّآ ءَالَ لُوطࣲۖ نَّجَّيۡنَٰهُم بِسَحَرࣲ‏
54:34.en: Indeed, We sent upon them a storm of stones, except the family of Lot - We saved them before dawn

54:35.ar: نِّعۡمَةࣰ مِّنۡ عِندِنَاۚ كَذَٰلِكَ نَجۡزِي مَن شَكَرَ
54:35.en: As favor from us. Thus do We reward he who is grateful

54:36.en: And he had already warned them of Our assault, but they disputed the warning

54:37.ar: وَلَقَدۡ رَٰوَدُوهُ عَن ضَيۡفِهِۦ فَطَمَسۡنَآ أَعۡيُنَهُمۡ فَذُوقُواْ عَذَابِي وَنُذُرِ
54:37.en: And they had demanded from him his guests, but We obliterated their eyes, [saying], "Taste My punishment and warning

54:38.en: And there came upon them by morning an abiding punishment

54:39.en: So taste My punishment and warning

54:40.ar: وَلَقَدۡ يَسَّرۡنَا ٱلۡقُرۡءَانَ لِلذِّكۡرِ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرࣲ‏
54:40.en: And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance, so is there any who will remember

54:41.en: And there certainly came to the people of Pharaoh warning

54:42.ar: كَذَّبُواْ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا كُلِّهَا فَأَخَذۡنَٰهُمۡ أَخۡذَ عَزِيزࣲ مُّقۡتَدِرٍ
54:42.en: They denied Our signs, all of them, so We seized them with a seizure of one Exalted in Might and Perfect in Ability

54:43.ar: أَكُفَّارُكُمۡ خَيۡرࣱ مِّنۡ أُوْلَٰٓئِكُمۡ أَمۡ لَكُم بَرَآءَةࣱ فِي ٱلزُّبُرِ
54:43.en: Are your disbelievers better than those [former ones], or have you immunity in the scripture

54:44.en: Or do they say, "We are an assembly supporting [each other]

54:45.en: [Their] assembly will be defeated, and they will turn their backs [in retreat]

54:46.ar: بَلِ ٱلسَّاعَةُ مَوۡعِدُهُمۡ وَٱلسَّاعَةُ أَدۡهَىٰ وَأَمَرُّ
54:46.en: But the Hour is their appointment [for due punishment], and the Hour is more disastrous and more bitter

54:47.en: Indeed, the criminals are in error and madness

54:48.ar: يَوۡمَ يُسۡحَبُونَ فِي ٱلنَّارِ عَلَىٰ وُجُوهِهِمۡ ذُوقُواْ مَسَّ سَقَرَ
54:48.en: The Day they are dragged into the Fire on their faces [it will be said], "Taste the touch of Saqar

54:49.en: Indeed, all things We created with predestination

54:50.ar: وَمَآ أَمۡرُنَآ إِلَّا وَٰحِدَةࣱ كَلَمۡحِۭ بِٱلۡبَصَرِ
54:50.en: And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye

54:51.ar: وَلَقَدۡ أَهۡلَكۡنَآ أَشۡيَاعَكُمۡ فَهَلۡ مِن مُّدَّكِرࣲ‏
54:51.en: And We have already destroyed your kinds, so is there any who will remember

54:52.en: And everything they did is in written records

54:53.en: And every small and great [thing] is inscribed

54:54.en: Indeed, the righteous will be among gardens and rivers

54:55.ar: فِي مَقۡعَدِ صِدۡقٍ عِندَ مَلِيكࣲ مُّقۡتَدِرِۭ
54:55.en: In a seat of honor near a Sovereign, Perfect in Ability

55:5.en: The sun and the moon [move] by precise calculation

55:6.en: And the stars and trees prostrate

55:7.en: And the heaven He raised and imposed the balance

55:8.en: That you not transgress within the balance

55:9.ar: وَأَقِيمُواْ ٱلۡوَزۡنَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ وَلَا تُخۡسِرُواْ ٱلۡمِيزَانَ
55:9.en: And establish weight in justice and do not make deficient the balance

55:10.en: And the earth He laid [out] for the creatures

55:11.en: Therein is fruit and palm trees having sheaths [of dates]

55:12.en: And grain having husks and scented plants

55:13.en: So which of the favors of your Lord would you deny

53:62.en: So prostrate to Allah and worship [Him]

u-5DNWrDKXA.speaker: adnan
u-5DNWrDKXA.speaker_note: his A Juz A Day series; welcomes viewers and teaches throughout in his own voice
u-5DNWrDKXA.title: A Juz A Day: 27th Juz - Allah Gives and Takes As He Pleases
u-5DNWrDKXA.one_line: Adh-Dhariyat, At-Tur, An-Najm, Al-Qamar and the opening of Ar-Rahman: Allah gives and takes as He wills, revelation is real, and punishment and mercy are certain.
u-5DNWrDKXA.summary: He frames the 27th juz around the idea that this is Allah's world: He gives and takes as He pleases. The two winds that open Adh-Dhariyat, one scattering and one carrying rain, illustrate this, followed by the stories of Ibrahim being given a son while the people of Lut, Pharaoh, Ad and Thamud are taken away. He describes the all-round believer who prays at night, seeks forgiveness before dawn, and gives intelligently to both the poor who ask and the poor who do not. At-Tur builds a chain of rhetorical questions that close every escape from the conclusion that Allah alone is worthy of worship, and promises that families of believers are reunited in paradise at the higher rank. In An-Najm he explains how revelation reached the Prophet through Jibril in his true form, ties the Sunnah to revelation, and draws out the core message shared with Musa and Ibrahim: no one carries another's burden and each person gets only what he strove for. Al-Qamar's repeated refrain about the Quran being easy to remember turns the destroyed nations into a question for every listener. He ends at the opening of Ar-Rahman, urging people to read it and connect the favours in the book with the favours around them.

outline.heading: Opening
The surahs of the 27th juz
outline.gist: The juz runs from Adh-Dhariyat to Al-Hadid; he starts from the beginning of Adh-Dhariyat for continuity.

outline.heading: Oaths by the winds: the promise is true
outline.gist: Allah swears by winds, clouds, ships and angels that the Judgment will come; the mockers who ask when it will be are told it is the day of their torment.

outline.heading: Allah gives and Allah takes
outline.gist: The scattering wind and the rain-bearing wind show that Allah grants and withdraws power and provision; realizing the world is not in our control leads to certainty about the Judgment.

outline.heading: Mercy always follows the mention of punishment
outline.gist: The righteous are in gardens and springs; the Quran pairs threat with mercy so we stay hopeful.

outline.heading: The all-round believer: night prayer, dawn forgiveness, smart giving
outline.gist: They sleep little, seek forgiveness before dawn without feeling superior, and give to both the poor who ask and the poor who do not.

outline.heading: As true as the fact that you speak
outline.gist: Human speech, with its genres, law, science and civilization, is unique to us; the revelation is just as certain.

outline.heading: Ibrahim's guests and the roasted calf
outline.gist: Ibrahim hurries to feed strangers and grows afraid when they do not eat, since assassins would refuse a host's food; they give him the news of a knowledgeable son.

outline.heading: Sarah's astonishment and the mission to Lut's people
outline.gist: Sarah wonders at a child in old age; Ibrahim asks the angels' real mission, which is to rain stones on Lut's town after saving its one believing household.

outline.heading: Musa, Ad, Thamud and Nuh: examples of taking away
outline.gist: Pharaoh was cast into the sea, Ad struck by a barren wind and Thamud by a blast, showing Allah takes as He pleases.

outline.heading: An expanding universe, a smoothed earth, pairs of all things
outline.gist: The heavens are built with might and expanding, and the earth is spread out and still beneath us, signs meant to bring awe.

outline.heading: Flee to Allah
outline.gist: Observing creation should produce awe of the Creator and lead to worship of Him alone.

outline.heading: Magician or madman: the same cliche across history
outline.gist: Every nation called its prophet the same names, not by collusion but because transgression produces the same response.

outline.heading: Keep reminding despite the loudmouths
outline.gist: The Prophet is not to blame for their rejection; reminders still benefit believers and those looking for faith.

outline.heading: Created only to worship Him
outline.gist: Allah needs no provision from us; worship is for our benefit, and He alone is the Provider.

outline.heading: What woe means
outline.gist: Wayl is a declaration of destruction, a word that recurs often in the last parts of the Quran.

outline.heading: At-Tur: the punishment is real, and a series of questions
outline.gist: He previews the surah's pattern: a vivid description of punishment and a run of rhetorical questions appealing to reason.

outline.heading: Oaths by the mount, the frequented house and the blazing sea
outline.gist: The house of the angels shows Allah does not need our worship, and the sea set ablaze on the Last Day is something to ponder.

outline.heading: The day of shaking: patient or not, it is the same
outline.gist: Those who amused themselves with falsehood are shoved into the fire, and complaining or enduring makes no difference to their punishment.

outline.heading: The righteous enjoy what their Lord gives
outline.gist: Gardens, bliss and reclining on thrones follow straight after the description of punishment.

outline.heading: Families reunited in paradise
outline.gist: Believing descendants are raised to the rank of their more devoted relatives without reducing anyone's reward, so families are reunited at the higher level.

outline.heading: What got them to paradise: fear and dua
outline.gist: Asked about their lives, the people of paradise say they feared Allah among their families and called on Him alone, a reminder to make dua for ourselves and our families.

outline.heading: Is he a poet? Did they make it up?
outline.gist: The rejection is not a product of intelligent minds but of not wanting to change; if the Quran is invented, let them produce one like it.

outline.heading: Created from nothing, or their own creators?
outline.gist: Each question escalates the impossibility until only one answer remains: Allah created them and alone deserves worship.

outline.heading: Even a falling piece of sky would not convince them
outline.gist: They would call it heaped clouds; Quraysh are warned of punishment in this world before the Judgment.

outline.heading: Be patient: you are under Our eyes
outline.gist: Dawah is a long game; glorify Allah when rising, at night and as the stars fade.

outline.heading: Your companion is not astray and does not speak from whim
outline.gist: The Prophet is someone they knew well; the Quran is Allah's words and the Sunnah in matters of religion is also from revelation, though not worldly matters.

outline.heading: Jibril in his true form on the horizon
outline.gist: The angel who fills the horizon came within two bow lengths; the majesty of the carrier shows the majesty of what he brought.

outline.heading: The second sighting at Sidrat al-Muntaha
outline.gist: During the Isra and Miraj the Prophet saw Jibril again at the furthest edge of creation, and his sight did not waver as he saw great signs.

outline.heading: Al-Lat, Al-Uzza and Manat: names you invented
outline.gist: Assigning daughters to Allah while disliking them is incoherent, and the idols are only inherited assumptions; humans do not get whatever they desire.

outline.heading: The good are rewarded with the best
outline.gist: Evildoers get the consequence of what they did, while doers of good receive the finest reward, far beyond their effort.

outline.heading: Avoid major sins despite minor slips
outline.gist: Small lapses do not cancel greatness; avoiding major and shameful sins does. Allah knew us as foetuses, so do not claim purity for yourselves.

outline.heading: The scriptures of Musa and Ibrahim: only what one strove for
outline.gist: No soul carries another's burden, and a person's life is the sum of their striving, which will be seen and fully rewarded.

outline.heading: He makes us laugh and cry, gives life and death
outline.gist: Joy and sorrow, life and death, wealth and poverty are all from Him; He is Lord of Sirius, the star they worshipped.

outline.heading: Destroyed nations and the same core message
outline.gist: Ad, Thamud, Nuh's people and the overturned cities; the message has always been justice, striving and accountability, and the Hour has drawn near.

outline.heading: Do you laugh instead of weeping? Prostrate
outline.gist: When the Prophet recited the end of An-Najm, even the disbelievers of Quraysh fell into prostration.

outline.heading: Al-Qamar: history as a glimpse of punishment
outline.gist: He points out the refrains about the Quran being easy to remember and how dreadful the punishment was, and the surah's distinctive rhyme.

outline.heading: The moon split and the swarming resurrection
outline.gist: Even the splitting of the moon was called magic; on the Day people will pour from graves like swarming locusts.

outline.heading: Nuh: the gates of the sky opened
outline.gist: Rain poured like an open door and the whole earth became a spring; it was Allah, not planks and nails, that carried the ark.

outline.heading: Ad and the furious wind
outline.gist: People were snatched up and left like uprooted palm trunks; the refrain asks if anyone will take heed.

outline.heading: Thamud and the she-camel
outline.gist: Sent a camel as a test with shared water, they killed it and were flattened by one blast.

outline.heading: Lut's people and Pharaoh's people
outline.gist: A storm of stones for one, while Lut's family was saved before dawn; Pharaoh's people seized in the grip of the Almighty.

outline.heading: Are you better than them, O Makkans?
outline.gist: No immunity is written for them, and their united front would be routed, which happened at Badr, with the Judgment even more bitter.

outline.heading: Everything created in measure; a single word
outline.gist: The order of creation shows it is no accident; every deed is recorded, and the righteous sit in the presence of the Sovereign.

outline.heading: Ar-Rahman: the first surah recited publicly
outline.gist: A companion recited it openly before Quraysh and was beaten nearly to death; its refrain asks which favours you will deny.

outline.heading: He taught the Quran and taught speech; the balance
outline.gist: Speech is a mercy unique to humans; the universe runs on a balance we must not corrupt, so weigh with justice; the earth is for all beings.

outline.heading: Read Ar-Rahman and connect the signs
outline.gist: He urges everyone to read the translation, observe the favours in the book and outside it, and arrive at glorifying the Lord of majesty and honour.

outline.heading: Outro

themes.label: Knowing Allah / relationship with Allah
themes.note: It is Allah's world: He gives and takes power, provision and life as He wills, which grounds certainty in the Judgment.

themes.label: Knowing Allah / relationship with Allah

hadith.gist: When the Prophet recited the end of Surah An-Najm, the disbelievers of Quraysh could not hold back and fell into prostration with the Muslims.

maxims: Allah gives and Allah takes; it is His world
Whenever He mentions punishment, He mentions mercy right after
Don't stop reminding because of a few loudmouths
Your life is the sum of what you strove for
Connect the signs in the book with the signs outside it

stories.who: Ibrahim and his angelic guests
stories.point: His instant generosity to strangers, and Allah giving him a son in old age, illustrate how Allah gives.

stories.who: A companion who first recited Ar-Rahman publicly in Makkah
stories.point: He was beaten almost to death but earned the honour of being the first to recite the Quran openly to Quraysh.

stories.who: Quraysh at Badr
stories.point: The promise that their united front would flee was fulfilled at the Battle of Badr.

contemporary: Expansion of the universe and the stillness of a rotating earth as modern observations matching the verses
takeaways: Accept that power, provision and outcomes are in Allah's hands and live with certainty about the Judgment
Pray at night, seek forgiveness before dawn, and look for the poor who do not ask
Make dua for your family and work toward being reunited with them in paradise
Avoid major and shameful sins and strive, knowing you get only what you work for
Read Ar-Rahman with its translation and connect its favours to the blessings around you

4:48.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ لَا يَغۡفِرُ أَن يُشۡرَكَ بِهِۦ وَيَغۡفِرُ مَا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ لِمَن يَشَآءُۚ وَمَن يُشۡرِكۡ بِٱللَّهِ فَقَدِ ٱفۡتَرَىٰٓ إِثۡمًا عَظِيمًا
4:48.en: Indeed, Allah does not forgive association with Him, but He forgives what is less than that for whom He wills. And he who associates others with Allah has certainly fabricated a tremendous sin

4:135.ar: ۞يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ كُونُواْ قَوَّٰمِينَ بِٱلۡقِسۡطِ شُهَدَآءَ لِلَّهِ وَلَوۡ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِكُمۡ أَوِ ٱلۡوَٰلِدَيۡنِ وَٱلۡأَقۡرَبِينَۚ إِن يَكُنۡ غَنِيًّا أَوۡ فَقِيرࣰ ا فَٱللَّهُ أَوۡلَىٰ بِهِمَاۖ فَلَا تَتَّبِعُواْ ٱلۡهَوَىٰٓ أَن تَعۡدِلُواْۚ وَإِن تَلۡوُۥٓاْ أَوۡ تُعۡرِضُواْ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ كَانَ بِمَا تَعۡمَلُونَ خَبِيرࣰ ا
4:135.en: O you who have believed, be persistently standing firm in justice, witnesses for Allah, even if it be against yourselves or parents and relatives. Whether one is rich or poor, Allah is more worthy of both. So follow not [personal] inclination, lest you not be just. And if you distort [your testimony] or refuse [to give it], then indeed Allah is ever, with what you do, Acquainted

43:81.ar: قُلۡ إِن كَانَ لِلرَّحۡمَٰنِ وَلَدࣱ فَأَنَا۠ أَوَّلُ ٱلۡعَٰبِدِينَ

Bip5d8MrOAU.speaker: adnan
Bip5d8MrOAU.speaker_note: fourth episode of his Muslim Wellness Network series; mentions his own clinical practice on the wards
Bip5d8MrOAU.title: The Philosophy of Islamic Thought #4: Ethical and Moral Philosophy of Islam
Bip5d8MrOAU.one_line: Islamic ethics as a theocentric, virtue-oriented, law-structured system that blends rules, character and consequences under an absolute commitment to righteousness.
Bip5d8MrOAU.summary: He argues that Islam starts its reform with morality because morality touches every part of life, unlike ideologies that begin from economics or the social contract. He defines Islamic ethics as theocentric, virtue-oriented and law-structured, grounded in revelation and rational accountability. Because Allah is the reference point, Muslim moral lines stay fixed while secular societies' lines drift, as with sexual ethics, and he links this to why shirk is unforgivable. Bringing Islam back means restoring its morals, not punishments. Islam is a hybrid of deontological, virtue and consequentialist ethics, shown through the organ-transplant dilemma, end-of-life care, the role of intention and the permitted exceptions to lying. Humans are morally responsible, rational agents with a fitrah and free will, and Sharia is a moral, legal and spiritual code. A moral code must cohere with a view of reality and of the good life, which atheistic frameworks cannot supply. He separates values, principles and ethical ranking, insisting justice outranks loyalty even against one's mother, and that righteousness carries infinite weight so ends never justify means. He closes by rejecting the split between private belief and public conduct and urges that youth learn cheating is wrong before fussing over details.

outline.heading: Opening
Islam begins its reform with morality
outline.gist: Capitalism, communism and liberalism start from one branch of life; morality touches everything, so Islam starts with the moral individual and society.

outline.heading: Epistemology first, then four disciplines
outline.gist: Every ideology must justify its knowledge; the series will cover morality, economics, wellbeing and governance.

outline.heading: The revival of Muslim philosophical writing
outline.gist: Such thinkers were once scarce and labelled deviant, a legacy of colonialism and Ottoman decline; the field is now maturing.

outline.heading: Definition: theocentric, virtue-oriented, law-structured
outline.gist: Revelation gives the principles like code, and reason applies them to every new situation; otherwise the Quran would need every scenario spelled out.

outline.heading: Theocentric: Allah as the reference point of good and evil
outline.gist: Secular morality follows society and drifts with war, media and culture; a Muslim dropped anywhere knows the same red lines.

outline.heading: Why shirk is unforgivable: a variable moral source
outline.gist: With more than one source of value the line in the sand keeps shifting; tawhid keeps morality constant.

outline.heading: Shifted lines in sexual ethics
outline.gist: Discussion itself has become impossible and identity is now tied to attraction; Islam cares about actions, not every desire needing fulfilment.

outline.heading: Bringing Islam back means bringing back its morals
outline.gist: Many imagine punishments and coercion; the real transformation the Companions found was ethical.

outline.heading: A sound moral code matters more than outward practice
outline.gist: He prefers someone weak in ritual with a solid moral ranking over someone praying while the moral code is broken.

outline.heading: Where good and evil come from
outline.gist: The sects differ on reason and revelation, a debate to enjoy not fight over; most moral codes worldwide trace back to revelation, and for Muslims the source is theocentric either way.

outline.heading: Three ethical schools and three questions
outline.gist: Rules, character and outcomes correspond to deontological, virtue and consequentialist ethics; Islam affirms inherent right and wrong.

outline.heading: Islam as a hybrid of all three
outline.gist: Islam accepts virtue ethics and a consequentialist awareness, but never pure utilitarianism, a mature system not yet named academically.

outline.heading: The transplant dilemma
outline.gist: Killing a dying patient to save five: rule and virtue ethics refuse, while utilitarian reasoning bends under need.

outline.heading: The Muslim answer and end-of-life care
outline.gist: A Muslim never hastens death; stopping treatment or relieving pain with a fatal side effect is not killing, because intention matters.

outline.heading: Intention and the violent pursuer
outline.gist: Courts already weigh intent; asked where a friend hides, rule ethics forbids lying while consequences point the other way.

outline.heading: Truthfulness and its exceptions
outline.gist: Compliments to a spouse, deceiving an enemy in war and reconciling people are not lying, but judging a contest is; lying to save the oppressed is allowed.

outline.heading: The human being: responsible, rational, fitrah, free will
outline.gist: Humans can go either way, reason ethically for themselves and carry an inner moral compass that abuse can corrupt.

outline.heading: Sharia as a moral, legal and spiritual code
outline.gist: Acts are judged by intention as well as outward conformity; moral psychology is embedded in law.

outline.heading: What is real: morality needs a coherent reality
outline.gist: Reality is created and sustained by a wise Creator; moral systems built on randomness collapse from incoherence.

outline.heading: Why be good if nothing follows?
outline.gist: Without accountability you cannot convince a poor person not to cheat; people want the moral code without the framework that makes it work.

outline.heading: The good life
outline.gist: Just conduct, cultivated virtue and conscious devotion leading to success in both lives; hedonism cannot explain altruism or moderation.

outline.heading: Values, principles and ethics
outline.gist: Values are what matter, principles are rules derived from them, ethics is the ranking used when values collide.

outline.heading: Your mother runs a red light: justice over loyalty
outline.gist: Truthful testimony is required even against parents; loyalty is a real virtue but never outranks justice.

outline.heading: The three core ethics and the infinite weight of righteousness
outline.gist: Righteousness generates justice and incorruptibility, and outweighs everything placed against it.

outline.heading: Pursuit of truth in belief and in people's rights
outline.gist: The Quran grounds worship in evidence, even saying the Prophet would worship a son if one existed; rights are sacred and never violated.

outline.heading: Ends never justify means: the straight path
outline.gist: Moral absolutism ignores outcomes; Muslims ask for a path, not a destination, and leave results to Allah.

outline.heading: Judge speakers by their ethics, not their fatwas
outline.gist: Fiqh choices are negotiable, but violating core ethics disqualifies a speaker; a mortgage fatwa does not.

outline.heading: No split between private belief and public conduct
outline.gist: Ethics runs continuously from prayer to contracts to governance; it is a way of life, not a department of it.

outline.heading: Teach youth that cheating is wrong first
outline.gist: Obsessing over halal details while cheating openly shows how far people are from the essence of the din.

ZA7FIIfzn24.speaker: adnan
ZA7FIIfzn24.speaker_note: continues his own values series and speaks of his personal struggle with forgiveness
ZA7FIIfzn24.title: The Values of Islam: Forgiveness and Pardoning (Maghfirah and 'Afw)
ZA7FIIfzn24.one_line: Forgiveness and pardoning are high ideals built on justice; on the 27th night, forgive others as you hope Allah forgives you.
ZA7FIIfzn24.summary: On the eve of the 27th night of Ramadan he turns to forgiveness and pardoning as they come from people, not from Allah. These are high-order ideals that the earlier ethics exist to protect: one cannot preach forgiveness where rights are violated, just as outward sunnah means nothing alongside eating haram. He lists the scholars' conditions for forgiveness: it must be for Allah, the wronged person must be capable of reclaiming the right, and it must lead to reconciliation rather than encouraging the wrongdoer. Asking the oppressed to forgive while their right is still held is shameful; forgiving what you cannot reclaim is weakness. Forgiveness means not seeking accountability and unloading a burden the wrongdoer has long forgotten, though distance may remain; pardoning goes further, restoring the relationship as if nothing happened. He tells of Abu Bakr resuming support of Mistah after the slander of Aishah when the Quran asked whether he did not love Allah's forgiveness, admitting he has not yet managed such forgiveness. He cites Ibrahim and Isa leaving their people to Allah's forgiveness, the Prophet's night spent on one verse, and the dua against grudges. He asks each listener to find someone to forgive tonight, stressing the choice is theirs.

outline.heading: Opening
Forgiving others on the 27th night
outline.gist: To obtain forgiveness on this night one must offer it to others; the talk concerns forgiveness from people, not from Allah.

outline.heading: Ideals that the basic ethics protect
outline.gist: Forgiveness and pardoning are high ideals of elegance that require justice and trustworthiness first; the series was ordered for this reason.

outline.heading: Ideals without foundations
outline.gist: Outward sunnah alongside haram earnings makes no sense; justice must be bolted down before calling the oppressed to forgive.

outline.heading: Condition of forgiveness: for the sake of Allah
outline.gist: Forgiveness is not a transaction or a favour to be returned later.

outline.heading: Condition of forgiveness: capability
outline.gist: One can only forgive a right one is able to reclaim; telling the oppressed to forgive while their right is still taken is shameful.

outline.heading: Condition of forgiveness: no harm
outline.gist: Forgive only when it brings reconciliation, not when it encourages the wrongdoer to keep transgressing.

outline.heading: Reclaim the right first
outline.gist: The Prophet told the companions to go after the wealth taken from them before choosing to forgive, since forgiving what you cannot reach is weakness.

outline.heading: Forgive those who do not hope for Allah's days
outline.gist: The Quran urges forgiving offenders because their reckoning is heavy; forgiveness goes against human nature and takes deliberate effort.

outline.heading: Forgiveness unloads your own burden
outline.gist: The wrongdoer forgets while the wronged carries the bitterness; forgiving cleanses the heart, though trust and distance may remain.

outline.heading: Pardoning restores the glass
outline.gist: 'Afw goes beyond forgiveness, returning the relationship to how it was, as the Prophet was told to pardon and say peace.

outline.heading: Abu Bakr, Aishah and Mistah
outline.gist: The slander devastated Abu Bakr, who swore to cut off support from Mistah, a relative he had been funding.

outline.heading: Do you not love that Allah forgives you?
outline.gist: The verse revealed after the slander moved Abu Bakr to restore Mistah's support for life.

outline.heading: Maybe tonight
outline.gist: He admits he has never managed to imagine forgiving like Abu Bakr and hopes each year this night will be the one.

outline.heading: Forgiveness is true strength and raises rank
outline.gist: Those who persevere and forgive show real resolve, and Allah only increases a servant in honour for pardoning.

outline.heading: Ibrahim and Isa leave their people to Allah
outline.gist: Both prophets entrusted sinners to Allah's forgiveness, and the Prophet spent a whole night reciting Isa's verse.

outline.heading: The Prophet carried no grudges
outline.gist: Pardoning differs from mercy, which is empathy, and from tawbah, which is changing oneself.

outline.heading: A dua against grudges
outline.gist: Later believers asked Allah to forgive those before them and remove any grudge from their hearts.

outline.heading: Most grievances are petty: let them go
outline.gist: Usually you could reclaim your right but it is not worth it, and living with the bitterness wastes your life; still, no one can force you to forgive.

outline.heading: Who do you need to forgive?
outline.gist: He asks each listener to find someone to forgive, especially those who never apologized, promising Allah will give more in return.

outline.heading: Allah loves to pardon
outline.gist: The Prophet's dua for these nights asks the One who loves pardoning; the question is whether we can do it ourselves.
